title: Basin-lake spring breeding pulse
scope: Qualitative biological productivity and overlapping spring breeding migrations in Project Hearthway's initial freshwater through-flow basin lake; usable within shared-setting ecology, seasonal planning, human subsistence development, and story development.
claims: The freshwater through-flow lake is biologically productive but spatially and seasonally varied.
The spring freshet creates seasonally favourable passage conditions from the sea and marks the start of the lake's seasonal rise in productivity.

An unnamed mass-breeding migrant arrives first and deposits dense ribbons or clusters of eggs onto sturdy plants and mineral surfaces across river-mouth shallows, protected bays, submerged ridges, and flooded vegetation margins rather than relying on one nursery ground.
Healthy adults generally return toward the sea after breeding, while the breeding-and-return cycle still carries meaningful adult mortality.
A distinct family-care migrant follows, remains through one warm season while rearing young, and escorts surviving young seaward before autumn storms and first freezes.
The family-care migrant's young consume the first migrant's eggs and juveniles as an important but non-exclusive food source.
Both migrants compete with resident lake fauna during their lake phases.
Humans, aquatic predators, terrestrial shore hunters, and bird-like fishing organisms exploit the seasonal abundance.
Reproductive risk is dispersed across places and times so that no single ordinary predator, flood, or fishery routinely destroys the entire generation.
Exceptional or compound recruitment failures remain possible.
The dispersed egg-deposition pattern creates feeding grounds that shift across the lake over the season.
boundaries: Freshet establishes a seasonal passage condition and productivity transition, not an exact hydraulic, salinity, sensory, or navigation mechanism. WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002 later establishes only a qualitative mixed outlet sequence; a favourable season can still contain dangerous peak flows, temporarily unusable micro-routes, crowding, ice, or debris.

Exact names, taxonomy, ancestry, size, cognition, sea range, route, timing, environmental cues, population scale, fecundity, exact egg-ribbon density, mortality, recruitment, carrying capacity, and return fidelity remain undefined. WLD-ECOLOGY-007 establishes only the mass breeder's foundational body plan, WLD-ECOLOGY-009 separately establishes the family-care migrant's foundational body plan and shelter–forage–regroup care interface, and WLD-ECOLOGY-010 later establishes only that migrant's qualitative outlet-passage choreography, while WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002 later supplies a candidate physical feature set against which it can be tested; their remaining anatomy and physiology, actual route use, and passage success remain undefined.
The number, dimensions, location, and biological composition of nursery habitats remain undefined beyond the qualitative habitat classes in the claims.
Egg deposition onto sturdy plants and mineral surfaces establishes no adhesion, entanglement, draping, anchoring, or other retention mechanism.
Flooded vegetation is not identified as the reserve-web guild or any other named flora.

Egg ribbons describe egg arrangement only and do not themselves establish a ribbon-shaped animal, body plan, or relationship to Lineage II ribbon forms; the mass breeder's selected foundation is governed separately by WLD-ECOLOGY-007.
Bird-like describes an ecological resemblance only and establishes no feathers, flight, Earth-bird anatomy, taxonomy, or named clade.
Human exploitation establishes a mortality channel, not a fishing technique, institution, law, ownership regime, trade, ritual, preservation method, or sustainable harvest.
No single ordinary predator, flood, or fishery routinely destroys the entire generation; this establishes no sustainable harvest rate and does not prevent exceptional or compound collapse.
Family care does not guarantee survival; the juvenile predator-prey link is important but non-exclusive, and no equilibrium or fixed annual return is established.

Adult repeat breeding, family-care reproductive mode, number or sex of carers, brood size, care behaviours beyond the shelter–forage–regroup pattern selected by WLD-ECOLOGY-009 and the bounded attempted regroup-and-advance sequence selected by WLD-ECOLOGY-010, diets beyond the selected prey link, disease, parasites, nutrient transfer, and carcass effects remain undefined.
The feeding grounds shift over the season, but their exact locations, timing, consumers, and movement pattern remain undefined.

WLD-ECOLOGY-007 establishes ordinary Mana-supported tissue reinforcement for the mass breeder only. Its exact Mana anatomy and mechanism, all specialised abilities, and the family-care migrant's Mana use remain undefined, as do creature progression, formal Skills, classes, levels, appraisal, and cultural or character knowledge.

These are ordinary living populations; no System spawning, seasonal reset, refill, pooled cohort identity, shared progression, loot rule, or automatic XP, attribute, trait, Skill, Mana, or power transfer is established.
story_implications: Spring and summer lake scenes can show changing migrant abundance, egg-bearing nursery areas, resident competition, concentrated predators, and human harvest activity without requiring either migrant to be a permanent lake resident.
The two migrants can expose the protagonist to distinct alien reproductive strategies before their anatomy, names, or full life cycles are known.
Seasonal abundance can affect access, danger, catches, predator movement, and local decisions, but any exact practice, institution, dispute, or crisis requires a later accepted record.
Author-side knowledge of the full cycle does not become automatic protagonist knowledge; each observation and inference requires an available source and bounded confidence.
system_implications: The selected breeding, egg deposition, hatching, care, predation, migration, mortality, and recruitment are ordinary world ecology under CAL0 WLD1.1D, WLD1.2D, and WLD2.1A+D, not a System change.
Egg ribbons, cohorts, seasonal aggregations, and family groups do not gain pooled System identity, levels, XP, Skills, classes, or rewards merely through proximity or coordination.
Predation and human harvest transfer no automatic XP, attributes, traits, Skills, Mana, levels, or power; any later material or magical effect requires its own mechanism and Author gate.
Seasonal arrival and recruitment remain finite and variable; there is no ambient spawning, encounter reset, harvest refill, guaranteed annual return, or automatic population recovery.
research_questions: Which parts of WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002's mixed outlet sequence provide usable bed or margin contact or lower-velocity pauses under which seasonal water states, and how do continuity, hydraulics, salinity transition, organism capability, and environmental sensing affect WLD-ECOLOGY-010 passage attempts without guaranteeing success?
What exact timing lets mass-breeder egg and juvenile availability overlap with the family-care migrant's juvenile demand?
What fecundity, mortality, predation, harvest, disease, and density-dependent recruitment budget can sustain both populations?
Which resident aquatic organisms compete with or consume each migrant life stage, and which shore and bird-like hunters exploit the pulse?

How do the mass breeder's remaining anatomy, life history, Mana pathway, System-eligible functions, and evolutionary relatives elaborate WLD-ECOLOGY-007, and how can the family-care migrant's WLD-ECOLOGY-009 foundation and WLD-ECOLOGY-010 passage choreography support its migration and care cycle?
What retention mechanism, if any, keeps eggs on sturdy plants and mineral surfaces, and how does it vary among nursery habitat classes without assuming a reserve-web relationship?
What do local people know, observe, harvest, preserve, regulate, contest, or misunderstand about the two migrations?
sources: Author selections across the guided lake productivity and migration design on 2026-08-14

author_approval.evidence: Across guided ecology questions on 2026-08-14, the Author selected a broadly productive but spatially and seasonally varied lake; proposed overlapping mass-breeding and family-care migrants; approved their juvenile predator-prey relationship and competition with resident fauna plus exploitation by humans and fishing land and bird-like organisms; and replied 'yes' to the spring-freshet sequence, one-warm-season rearing cycle, and the presented recommendation for dense ribbons or clusters of eggs deposited onto sturdy plants and mineral surfaces across dispersed nursery belts.
